chapter: Henry Kimball and the Kimball family
title: Andrew Kimball and the Kimball brothers
summary: Discovering that trumpeter Andrew Kimball was his father's brother, and the singing quartet of brothers.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, I think I would, uh, I've heard that he was no relation to your family. Is that true, or, uh?
He was. He was? Yes, that was my father's brother.
Oh, I didn't know. Oh, I heard he was no relation. Somebody told me he was no relation. I didn't know. Uh.

So, I should have known. I didn't know that they were related until after I had started to play music. And I met Andrew Kimball and Mrs. Margaret Kimball in Shreveport. And Bill Matthews, the trombone player, came to me and told me that he wanted to, that Mr. Kimball wanted to talk with me. And I went over and he asked me about, did I know my father's father? And I told him, yes, I know him. And he asked what was his name. I said his name was Henry Kimball also. That's your grandfather's name. Yes. And, uh, he asked whether or not, uh, I might be mistaken because, uh, they were four brothers. It was Ed, Benny, Henry, and James.
Did the other brothers play any instruments?
No. No. No. They, that group of brothers had a quartet.
They sang. They did sing them. Yeah. By the way, did your grandfather, Henry Kimball, play any instruments? No. He didn't play anything. Or sing or instruments?
